analysis.title: Hot October CPI likely locks in December hike
key_insights: October CPI came in hotter than expected: headline +0.4% MoM vs 0.3% expected, core +0.3% MoM vs 0.2% expected. YoY figures are unavailable because of missing October 2025 data from last year's government shutdown.
CA-CIB sees the October CPI as a genuinely strong report because volatile categories contributed less than in recent months, so there was less noise in the number.

After the CPI and hawkish Fedspeak, markets fully price a December hike, with about a 10% chance of a 50bp move. Total additional tightening priced by September 2027 is about 75bp, up from just below 50bp at the end of the prior week.

Governor Waller said a 50bp hike should be considered in December if October CPI was similar to the past two monthly readings (core around 0.3% or higher), and that a 25bp hike alone would put the Fed's credibility at risk. This is a shift from a month earlier, when he said hikes did not need to come at consecutive meetings.
Dallas Fed President Logan said the Fed may be able to move more rapidly this winter than it has this fall, then pause after two more hikes. CA-CIB reads this as pointing to consecutive hikes.

CA-CIB does not think the broader Committee has reached the bar for a jumbo hike. It sees a real and growing possibility of hikes at consecutive meetings in December and January, versus its base case of December and March.
CA-CIB suggests Waller's 50bp comment may partly be an attempt to jawbone the market against a further repricing lower of Fed hikes, rather than a true base case.

CA-CIB questions why the Fed held in October rather than hiking 25bp, which CA-CIB had argued was the better approach. It wants the October FOMC minutes (Wednesday 14:00 ET) to lay out the rationale for the pause more clearly than Chair Warsh did in his press conference.
CA-CIB forecasts October retail sales at 0.0% MoM headline (vs 0.8% in September, which was flattered by gas prices), 0.2% ex-auto and 0.3% ex-auto and gas. Consensus is 0.1%/0.3%/0.4%.
CA-CIB expects October import prices of +0.7% MoM (September +1.1%), with strength outside energy from AI-buildout products. It does not see this as a game changer for consumer inflation.
CA-CIB forecasts October industrial production at -0.1% MoM (utilities drag from mild weather) vs +0.7% in September, and manufacturing production at +0.2% vs +0.3%.

CA-CIB expects UofM sentiment to rise to 54.0 from 51.0 on lower gas prices and hopes for an end to the Iran war after the midterms. That would be the highest since July but still historically very low.
CA-CIB forecasts October housing starts +4.8% MoM to 1,280k and building permits -1.6% to 1,375k, a third straight monthly decline in permits.

CA-CIB's macro forecast: 2.3% GDP growth in 2026 (cut from 2.5% because of the Iran war) and 2.1% in 2027. Headline CPI peaks at 4.2% YoY in May 2026. Core CPI hovers around 2.6-2.8% through early 2027. Hikes of 25bp each in December and March would take the upper bound to 4.50%, followed by two 25bp cuts in Q4 2027 to 4.00%.

Democrats performed strongly in the midterms, but CA-CIB cautions that the filibuster and presidential veto may keep legislative gridlock largely in place. The outcome could affect the AI buildout and the Iran war.

risk_factors: A hot CPI and hawkish Fedspeak could push the Fed to consecutive hikes or a 50bp move.
Persistently high inflation, with Iran war energy spikes adding upside risk to forecasts.
Import prices elevated by AI-buildout goods.
Possible regulations slowing the AI buildout after the midterms.
The K-shaped economy, with growth concentrated in AI investment.
AI replacing jobs could weigh on the labour market.
vol_and_positioning: Fed funds futures pricing shifted: a December hike is fully priced with about a 10% chance of 50bp, and about 75bp of additional hikes are priced by September 2027, up from just below 50bp at the end of the prior week and from a peak of nearly 100bp earlier.
geopolitical: The Iran war has caused a surge in gas prices, a drag on consumers, and upside risk to inflation forecasts.
Hopes for an end to the Iran war after the midterms could lift consumer sentiment.
Democrats' strong midterm performance could affect the AI buildout and the Iran war, though gridlock from the filibuster and presidential veto may constrain them.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish Fedspeak and a hot CPI could produce a 50bp hike in December, or hikes at consecutive meetings in December and January. Waller backs 50bp if core CPI stays near 0.3%.
tension_points.bear_case: CA-CIB does not think the broader Committee has reached the bar for a jumbo hike. Waller's 50bp comment may be partly jawboning, and a sharp oil drop plus possible AI regulation could ease inflation.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A cooler core CPI or a lack of other FOMC members backing 50bp, as the October FOMC minutes and further Fedspeak will show.

theme_stances.key_argument: A real and growing possibility the Fed delivers hikes at consecutive meetings in December and January instead of December and March.
theme_stances.evidence: a real and growing possibility that the Fed could opt to deliver hikes at consecutive meetings
